sources.headline: Death toll rises in Ukraine after Russia attacks aid centre, hospice and hospital
sources.text: Russian strikes on Ukraine – including on an aid centre, a hospice and a hospital – have killed at least 38 civilians and injured scores of others over the last 24 hours.At least 33 people are known to have died in a glide bomb attack in the southern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday night, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said the number of victims was set to rise as more than 50 people could be trapped under the rubble.He called the strike in Komyshuvakha village "one of the largest mass killings committed by Russia during this war".Ukraine had proposed to extend and expand last week's ceasefire in the Kherson region which allowed people from the frontline Russian-occupied town of Oleshky to evacuate, Zelensky added.The attack on a school building being used as an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha was Moscow's response, he said.Elsewhere, a hospice was attacked in the central city of Dnipro and a hospital was hit in the north-eastern city of Kharkiv, where Zelensky said 73 people were wounded, most of them elderly patients.Nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit Komyshuvakha as residents were gathering to receive humanitarian aid at a distribution centre, authorities said. Local media reported that when the attack began, people took refuge underground but the roof collapsed, trapping many underneath. "The scale of the tragedy is difficult to comprehend," regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.Russia's defense ministry said the attack had targeted Ukrainian military units and killed 25 servicemen. However, there was no credible evidence that the site was being used by the Ukrainian military and there were no major military or industrial facilities in the settlement of Komyshuvakha, reports BBC News Russian defence correspondent Ilya Abishev.The village is to the south-east of the city of Zaporizhzhia, which has come under constant Russian bombardment. According to Abishev, Komyshuvakha is of high military importance as part of Ukraine's defensive and transport network on the approaches to the regional capital. But the UN's human rights monitoring mission said the distribution of humanitarian aid at the local school had been highly publicised and the attack "seems to have violated the most fundamental principles of international humanitarian law", external."I realise that I am violating ethics," wrote Filatov. "I want as many people as possible to see these photos. Especially politicians and diplomats. Especially abroad."These are elderly, terminally ill people. This is a Russian missile."Elsewhere in Dnipro, a separate strike killed two people and left 18 others wounded. Another five people were killed in aerial bomb and drone strikes on Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region.Russia has also struck energy infrastructure in nine regions, affecting water and heating. The water supply in Kyiv was entirely cut off "due to enemy attacks and damage to the capital's energy infrastructure", the main water supplier Kyivvodokanal said. The entire metro network was suspended on Tuesday and Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the situation surrounding the city's power supply was becoming "very difficult".As Ukraine was counting its dead, the Kremlin announced it would take part in three-way peace talks with Ukraine brokered by the US in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November.It will be the first trilateral meeting since February. Since then, Russia and the US have begun engaging more directly, with US President Donald Trump announcing a deal to import Russian diesel.Speaking to reporters in Berlin on Tuesday, Zelensky said that it was important for Russia to engage seriously in negotiations on a ceasefire and a peaceful settlement, but that he had so far had not seen "any indication" of that being the case.Several rounds of ceasefire talks late last year yielded no results, and in public declarations Russian officials have generally refused to budge from Moscow's maximalist demand of effective Ukrainian surrender.US First Lady Melania Trump Melania Trump, who was credited with brokering a truce last week in the besieged town of Oleshky, is set to host representatives of Russia and Ukraine at the White House on Thursday. However, no details were given in the White House statement of who was due to attend the meeting., externalThe UN said last month that civilian casualties in Ukraine had reached a "record level", as Russian armed forces resumed systematic attacks on energy infrastructure.Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Its advances on the front line have since stalled, and attacks on Ukraine have intensified, with Moscow employing large numbers of missiles and drones to strike Ukrainian cities. At the same time, Ukraine is faces a critical air defense shortage due to stalled Western deliveries of weapons and a lack of American Patriot interceptor missiles.In Berlin, Zelensky acknowledged that although the front line was stable "the situation in the air was not as positive, particularly when it comes to our air defence capabilities and the protection of our civilian population".

sources.headline: Death toll hits 29 after Russian strike on Ukrainian aid site, with 48 still missing
sources.text:
In this photo provided by the Ukrainian Emergency Service, rescuers evacuate a wounded civilian from a residential building after Russian air attack in Dnipro, Ukraine, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026.
Ukrainian Emergency Service/via AP
hide caption
Ukrainian Emergency Service/via AP
KYIV, Ukraine — The death toll from a Russian attack in southern Ukraine on a site where people had gathered to receive humanitarian aid rose to 29 on Tuesday, with 48 still missing, as a wave of overnight strikes targeted power plants across the country, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people.
Dozens of rescuers and volunteers continued to search the cratered blast site of a destroyed aid facility and shelter in Komyushuvakha, a village in Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia region, hoping to find missing residents alive under the rubble. Instead, more bodies were pulled out and carried away in white plastic sheeting. "The scale of the tragedy is terrifying," Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the region's military administration, wrote in an online post. "This is one of the worst tragedies in terms of the number of civilian victims in our region since the start of the full-scale war."
A woman and her cat take shelter from a Russian drone and missile attack, in a metro station, now used as a bomb shelter, in Kyiv, Ukraine, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026.
Danylo Antoniuk/AP
hide caption
Danylo Antoniuk/AP
Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, triggering emergency power cuts, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections.
"The Russians think America won't notice this signal of theirs," he said. "But we need to notice and stop such terror. We need to help Ukraine defend its skies; otherwise, Russia will never stop its missile strikes." Three days of mourning were declared in Zaporizhzhia where Russian bunker-busting bombs, filled with nearly 1.5 tons of explosives, were used in Monday's attack. The dead included four police officers and two rescue workers, Semikin said Tuesday. At least five people were hurt.
In this photo provided by the Ukrainian Emergency Service, a residential building is seen following a Russian air attack in Dnipro, Ukraine, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026.
Ukrainian Emergency Service/via AP
hide caption
Ukrainian Emergency Service/via AP
In the northeast region of Kharkiv, a combined Russian missile and drone attack wounded at least 62 people, local authorities said. A strike damaged a medical facility in the Nemyshlianskyi district, shattered windows in four apartment buildings and damaged cars. More than 200 patients were transferred to other medical facilities, head of the regional military administration Oleh Syniehubov said. In the Dnipro area, rescuers pulled a woman alive from the rubble Tuesday morning, after a Russian attack killed one person and wounded 17, local authorities said. The attack damaged an outpatient clinic and a hospital. Patients were transferred to other hospitals, Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, said. Russia's Ministry of Defense said Tuesday that it had shot down 856 Ukrainian drones overnight. Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 493 drones were fired toward the Russian capital.
A Ukrainian drone attack wounded two employees at an oil refinery in the Russian city of Yaroslavl, regional Gov. Mikhail Yevrayev said Tuesday. He added that there was damage to the refinery's infrastructure. Rolling blackouts have been instituted in the south, west and east of Russian-occupied Crimea following attacks on energy infrastructure, Moscow-installed officials said Tuesday.

sources.headline: Russia's 'vile terrorist strike' kills dozens at school used as aid centre
sources.text: Ukranian President Volodymyr Zelenskky has described a series of deadly Russian attacks at a school being used as an aid hub in the country's south-eastern region of Zaporizhzhia, as a "vile terrorist strike". At least 33 people have been killed, and 50 people remain buried in the rubble following the attack, Mr Zelenskyy said in Berlin on Tuesday, local time. Earlier, Regina Kharchenko, secretary of the Zaporizhzhia City Council, said 27 people were missing. The school, bordering the frontline of Russia's four-and-a-half-year war with Ukraine, was being used as a shelter.Ukrainian servicemen open fire to shoot down a Russian drone at the site of the attack. (Reuters)Mr Zelenskyy said the school was no longer used for classes, but was used to deliver aid to residents in the area every Monday. He claimed Russian forces could not have been unaware that the school was being used."The Russians struck first just as people were arriving — a few aerial bombs," Mr Zelenskyy said. "Then there was a second strike — more air bombs, this time on the shelter. A vile terrorist strike."Two members of a rescue crew and four police officers were among those killed, emergency services said, after Russia launched the double-tap strike. Two rescue workers were among those taken to hospital for treatment.Russia and Ukraine both deny deliberately targeting civilians in the conflict.The Russian Defence Ministry said the attack had targeted Ukrainian military units in areas around Komyshuvakha and two other settlements in the Zaporizhzhia region.It said in a statement on Tuesday that up to 25 Ukrainian servicemen had been killed, while 15 vehicles and an electronic warfare station were also destroyed.In August, UN monitors said that casualties have risen sharply from last year, adding that more civilians were killed or injured in the war in Ukraine in July than in any month since March 2022.Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha also condemned the attack."Another barbaric and cynical Russian attack," he said. "Russia's cruelty knows no bounds, and its disregard for human life has no moral justification."The aftermath of the attack. (Reuters)Citing the attack, Mr Sybiha urged countries to shun Russian participation in top-level sport following a ruling by sport's highest court ordering the country's reinstatement in major tournaments."Russia deserves condemnation, isolation, and consequences, not a return to international respectability," Mr Sybiha wrote on X. "Its crimes cannot be separated from its flag, its national teams, or its attempts to regain international legitimacy."Photographs posted online showed smouldering rubble strewn throughout the area.The attack occurred a day after the expiry of a six-day local ceasefire arranged to bring aid into Oleshky to the south-west in Kherson region and evacuate residents wishing to leave.US-mediated peace talks are scheduled to take place in Abu Dhabi on November 10 to 11.Reuters

sources.headline: Russian bombing of Ukrainian aid centre kills 26 people
sources.text: Russian forces have bombed an aid centre in Ukraine, killing at least 31 people, according to Ukrainian officials, as the United States announced plans for new peace talks on November 10 and 11.The aid centre, at a school in the village of Komyshuvakha in the Zaporizhzhia region, had been closed to students because the village sits too close to the front line, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday. Instead, it served as a shelter and as a weekly distribution point for aid packages, which residents who remain in the village collected every Monday.Recommended Stories list of 4 itemslist 1 of 4Kherson braces for return of war as localised Russia-Ukraine truce endslist 2 of 4Russia, Ukraine air raid alert apps hit by cyberattacks after truce endslist 3 of 4Nuclear radiation in Russia, Ukraine? No, just hacked warning alertslist 4 of 4Suspected cyberattacks trigger supermarket fridge failures across Europeend of list“The Russians struck first just as people were arriving – a few aerial bombs,” he said in his nightly address. “Then there was a second strike – more air bombs, this time on the shelter. A vile terrorist strike.”Zelenskyy said the Russians could not have been unaware that residents remaining in Komyshuvakha gathered each week to pick up humanitarian packages.Among the dead were two members of a rescue crew and four police officers, according to Ukraine’s emergency services. Five people, including two rescue workers, were being treated in hospitals.Photographs posted online showed smouldering debris scattered across the area.Warnings of new ‘massive attack’There was no immediate comment from Russia.Zelenskyy said the attack was “further proof that Russia does not want any kind of de-escalation, any real justice.”He argued that Moscow had squandered an opening created by a humanitarian mission last week in Oleshky, a Russian-occupied southern city, which was brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump.“If Russia genuinely wanted de-escalation, there was an opportunity following the situation in Oleshky to continue taking humanitarian steps,” he said. “We proposed this. But Russia continues to kill people.”Zelenskyy also said Ukrainian intelligence had warned that Russia was preparing a new “massive attack” on the country’s energy and logistics networks, timed to coincide with the US midterm elections on Tuesday.Writing on X, he said Moscow was counting on the world’s attention being elsewhere, allowing Ukraine’s struggles with air defences and Patriot missiles to go unnoticed.He urged Washington to pressure Russia “in such a way that it has no alternative but to end this war”.Talks in Abu DhabiHours after the attack, US special envoy Steve Witkoff said that delegations from Ukraine and Russia would meet in Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates, on November 10 and 11.In a social media post, Witkoff said the talks would address “post-war security agreements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures, and ending the war”.Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to the new round of three-way talks after meeting Witkoff in St Petersburg on October 21.The talks come as US negotiators seek a breakthrough before winter in the war, now in its fifth year.The last US-mediated talks were held in February, before the US and Israel launched their war on Iran.Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, cited Monday’s attack in urging countries to oppose Russia’s return to elite international sport, after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ordered that Russia be reinstated in major ice hockey tournaments.“Russia deserves condemnation, isolation, and consequences, not a return to international respectability,” Sybiha wrote on X.Elsewhere in Ukraine on Monday, drone strikes injured 12 people in the eastern Kharkiv region, damaging a refrigeration facility, greenhouses and homes, according to emergency services. In the Black Sea port of Odesa, five people were injured when a warehouse was hit and nearby houses were damaged.Russia’s Ministry of Defence said its forces had shot down 212 Ukrainian drones overnight. The governor of Russia’s Samara region, Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, said air defences had repelled an attack there but gave no further details.

sources.headline: Ukraine says hopes of 'progress toward peace' knocked by attack on aid distribution centre
sources.text:
Published on 2 November 2026 - 19:34 GMT+1•Updated
3 November 2026 - 7:52 GMT+1
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said any hopes of "progress toward peace" following a localised truce last week had been dampened by deadly Russian strikes on an aid distribution centre in southeastern Ukraine.
The aerial bomb attack in the region of Zaporizhzhia killed at least 26 people, including two rescue workers and four police officers, on Monday, according to Ukraine's State Emergency Service (DSNS). Five others were also reportedly injured in the strikes.
Ivan Fedorov, the regional governor, said Russian forces had fired "at least nine KAB-3000 bombs" on the Komyshuvakha settlement throughout the day.
"All emergency services are working flat out at the scene, while municipal workers are clearing the rubble," he wrote in a post on Telegram.
Zelenskyy called it an "utterly horrific" attack, saying it had targeted "a school used for humanitarian purposes" where some people were receiving aid.
"After the first aerial bomb strike, there was a double-tap strike with nine more bombs, specifically targeting the shelter where people were taking cover," he wrote on X.
Images shared by the DSNS from the scene show a building reduced to a pile of rubble and what appears to be a burned-out bus.
Russia 'counting on more killings'
In his post, Zelenskyy said the attacks had also knocked hopes of moving closer to a peace deal.
"After the humanitarian operation in Oleshky, there was a moment when the next steps could have shown that progress toward peace was possible," he wrote. Evacuees from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in Ukraine's southern Kherson region arrived in Ukraine on Saturday after travelling through Belarus amid a rare humanitarian truce between Kyiv and Moscow.
But Zelenskyy said the Zaporizhzhia attack showed Russia was "sending an entirely opposite signal" and that it was "counting on more killings."
"There must be a response to this – a response from the world. A strong and tough response," he added.
Authorities in Kherson said Russia had resumed attacks on the region on Monday following a drone strike on the Korabelny district.
A 62-year-old woman and a 73-year-old man reportedly sustained blast injuries in the attack.

Published: 3:06am, 3 Nov 2026Updated: 10:14am, 3 Nov 2026

Russian forces on Monday bombed a school being used as an aid distribution point in a village in Ukraine’s southeastern Zaporizhzhia region, killing 26 people, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and the country’s emergency services said.

The emergency services said two members of a rescue crew and four police ‌officers were among the dead in the village of Komyshuvakha. Five people were being treated in hospital, including two rescuers.

Zelensky, in his nightly video address, said Russian forces initially dropped aerial bombs on a school in the village, used as a shelter and for distributing humanitarian assistance every Monday.

There were no classes at the school, he said, as the village, lying southeast of the region’s main city, also called Zaporizhzhia, was too close to the front line in the 4½-year-old war.

“The Russians struck first just as people ⁠were arriving – a few aerial bombs,” he said. “Then there was a second strike – more air bombs, this time on the shelter. A vile terrorist strike.”

Zelensky ‌said the Russians could not have been unaware that residents remaining in Komyshuvakha gathered each week to pick up humanitarian packages.

Efforts to rescue people were hindered as Russian drones launched additional attacks in the area. Photo: Reuters

The attack, he said, had shown that Moscow was intent ‌on killing people instead of building on the past week’s humanitarian mission in the embattled southern city of Oleshky, brokered by US ⁠first lady Melania Trump.

“Russians ⁠continue to demonstrate, time and again, their hatred of Ukraine and everything that exists here,” he said.

“If Russia genuinely wanted de-escalation, there was an opportunity following the situation in ‌Oleshky to continue taking humanitarian steps. We proposed this. But Russia continues to kill people.”

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, citing the attack, urged countries to shun Russian participation in top-level sport following a ‌ruling ‌by sport’s highest court ordering the country’s reinstatement in major tournaments.

“Russia deserves condemnation, isolation, and consequences, not a return to international respectability,” Sybiha ‌wrote on X. “Its crimes cannot be separated from its flag, its national teams, or its attempts to regain international legitimacy.”

Regina Kharchenko, secretary of the ⁠Zaporizhzhia City Council, said 27 people were missing in the attack.

Zaporizhzhia region police said officers and rescue teams were trying to reach residents believed ⁠to be trapped under rubble.

Photographs posted online showed smouldering rubble strewn throughout the area.

The attack occurred a day after the expiry of a six-day local ceasefire arranged to bring aid into Oleshky to the southwest in Kherson region and evacuate residents wishing ‌to leave.

In Washington, a senior US official ‌told Reuters that the US will bring together delegations from Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on November 10 to 11 to discuss moves towards ending the war, post-war security agreements and de-escalation.

US negotiators have been seeking a breakthrough before winter in the long-running conflict. The last US-mediated peace talks took place in February before the US and Israel launched a war against Iran.

sources.headline: Ukraine says Russian strikes dash peace progress hopes after 26 killed
sources.text: KYIV - Ukraine on Nov 2 said multiple Russian strikes on a school where humanitarian aid was distributed killed at least 26 people and dashed fragile hopes of “progress toward peace” after a local ceasefire in the south expired without violations.Russia resumed its strikes on the southern region of Kherson after the end of a local ceasefire in the area, the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours since Russia’s 2022 invasion, Kyiv said.A rare pause in the fighting, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump to enable a mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, ended on Nov 1, with neither side reporting breaches.But hours after the truce, Russia targeted a village in Zaporizhzhia, adjacent to Kherson, with repeated strikes that killed at least 26 people, the acting regional governor said. Some of the dead had come to collect aid at a local school.Footage posted by the Ukrainian emergency services showed the building reduced to piles of smouldering rubble and rescuers working at the site.“Every Monday humanitarian aid was distributed to people there. The Russians carried out the first strike just as people arrived – several aerial bombs. Then there was a repeat strike – more aerial bombs, this time targeting the shelter,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in his daily address.Among those killed were “two rescue workers and four police officers”, acting regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Telegram.The service named the rescuers as two 44-year-olds: Denys Konovalenko and Oleksy Sushchevsky.“Every day they went out to help people, working in dangerous conditions and risking their own lives to save others,” it said in a statement.Zelensky said that after the Oleshky truce, “there was a moment when the next steps could have shown that progress toward peace was possible.”“With these killings, Russia is sending an entirely opposite signal: Russia is counting on more killings. There must be a response to this”.Russia fortifies positionsThe ceasefire last week enabled an evacuation of the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky.It was the longest pause in fighting between the neighbours in the war, now in its fifth year, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.A senior Ukrainian figure told AFP on Nov 1 that Russia refused a Ukrainian offer to extend the truce.Kyiv’s military also alleged that Moscow had used the pause in fighting to “fortify its positions”.The Kremlin did not deny the accusations, with its spokesman Dmitry Peskov telling reporters on Nov 2: “This is a completely normal practice in such situations.”He alleged the Ukrainian army had also used pauses in fighting in the past to regroup.Moscow saw the Oleshky humanitarian mission as “successful”, Peskov added, praising the “good cooperation between all sides” and singling out the role of its human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova.Lantratova oversaw the ceasefire alongside her Ukrainian counterpart Dmytro Lubinets in one of the most substantial instances of Russian-Ukrainian cooperation since the start of the war.The mission saw people taken both to Ukraine-controlled territory and to Moscow-annexed Crimea.The Kremlin said that no other similar missions were being planned “at the moment”.US-led talks between Russia and Ukraine are set to resume in November.US President Donald Trump has pushed for a settlement to the dragging war but efforts have not yet led to a breakthrough.The talks – expected to be held in Abu Dhabi – come as Kyiv and its European allies worry that Trump has increasingly sided with Moscow.CyberattacksBoth Russia and Ukraine said overnight that their emergency warnings apps were hacked in apparent cyberattacks that came after the truce had ended.Ukraine said it suspected its air raid alert system had been compromised, after baseless alerts of a radiation threat were sent to millions.The warning system provides vital information about incoming Russian drones and missiles.Russia has intensified its attacks this year, firing ballistic missiles and fast jet-powered drones, both of which are hard to intercept.Moscow said that an app belonging to its emergency situations ministry that also warns of attacks had been hacked, too.The app is not widely used in Russia, where warnings of Ukrainian drone attacks are not as common and typically sent by text message in border regions. AFP
